text:
emma: Heads-up — dedicated canary for customer Atlas Health just showed a large p95 step-up (~2.4x) right after the 2026-03-15 merge. Blocking the rollout until we triage.
raj: saw alerts. p50 fine, p95 and p99 spike across long-seq traffic (>8k tokens).
olivia: looks like kernel selection changes landed in PR #5012 earlier today (scheduler/batching heuristic). Could be related.
sam: deploy-bot reported canary failed health checks: `deploy-bot: canary 25/30 failed p95>2000ms`
deploy-bot: Canary deployment halted automatically by autoscaler policy.
perf-ci: CI/perf-tests flagged a regression on dedicated smoke: `latency-regression: +128% p95` on heavy-seq profile.
emma: Can someone attach a minimal repro? Need stack/profile samples.
raj: repro steps (local repro):
```
# simulate atlas workload
python load.py --model-variant dense-quant --seq-dist heavy --concurrency 12 --tokens 12000
# observe p95
```
raj: profiler snapshot (wall time, short):
```
select_kernel_for_batch  42%
KVCache::get_or_prefetch  28%
BatchScheduler::try_merge   12%
tensor_copy_async          6%
other                      12%
```
olivia: interesting — select_kernel_for_batch dominated. PR #5012 added a new heuristic that favors tiny-batch hotpath on mix workloads; maybe misclassifying long sequences and forcing a 'slow' kernel.
sam: I see increased mutex contention around KVCache eviction in the flame trace. Not sure if it's the kernel path or eviction timing.
josh: linking a log excerpt: `kv_eviction_latency_ms: p95=310 -> 910` post-merge. Also observed more scheduler hops (requests moving between queues).
oncall: oncall opened INC-2026-0315: "Dedicated canary p95 step-up — rollout blocked" and paged eng-runtime.
emma: Good. Let's bisect quickly. Can someone run `git bisect` between pre-PR merge and current?
olivia: started a bisect on the runtime branch. Initial suspect list: #4971 (batching heuristics), #5012 (scheduler hints), #4999 (kv-prefetch timing tweak).
perf-ci: quick CI run shows commit 8a9f3d (PR #5012 merge) introduced the regression when running heavy-seq perf harness.
raj: confirmed locally — checking out 8a9f3d reproduces spike, reverting that commit brings p95 back to baseline.
sam: repro with revert patch:
```
git revert 8a9f3d --no-commit
make -C runtime test-perf-heavyseq
# p95 back to normal
```
emma: Do we revert the merge in main or hotfix? What's impact surface?
josh: PR #5012 also improved small-batch throughput for interactive customers; reverting will hurt some customers. Need a targeted hotfix: disable the new tiny-batch hint for dedicated deployments or skip it for long-seq requests.
olivia: quick patch idea: short-circuit the heuristic when avg_seq_len > 2k or when KV hit-rate < 0.7. I can draft and test.
oncall: customers on dedicated receiving degraded experience: Atlas reported errors at 14:32 UTC, SLA risk if not resolved within 2 hours.
emma: priority: patch, test, canary. If patch fails then full revert.
perf-ci: also observed CI perf flaky on GPUs with mixed workloads — added test-case at CI stage to catch this.
raj: experimenting with selective kernel override: force heavyseq -> legacy_kernel. Preliminary results: p95 -> baseline, increased cost ~6%.
sam: add telemetry flag to runtime: `disable_tiny_batch_hint` that we can flip via rollout config for dedicated customers.
josh: I'll coordinate with releases to prepare hotfix branch and hold main revert if patch passes canary.
emma: action items: olivia to open PR with heuristic guard + unit tests (ETA 30m), raj to run extended repro load (ETA 20m), josh to prepare hotfix branch and rollback plan, sam to update canary config flag in deployment.
olivia: PR opened: runtime#5028 (heuristic-guard-longseq). Linking logs and perf runs in the PR.
perf-ci: perf run on PR5028 shows p95 delta: -80% vs broken main, +3% vs pre-merge baseline.
emma: good signals. Kick canary once all checks pass.
oncall: paging update: monitoring shows p95 trending down after staging canary started.
deploy-bot: Canary promotion paused until 3 successful minutes.
emma: If canary stable, proceed with hotfix release and patch main to avoid subsequent rollouts picking up bug.
josh: I'll notify Atlas CS and ask them to validate.
olivia: leaving notes in PR about root cause: kernel-hint misclassification on long sequences combined with KV eviction thrash. Suggest follow-ups: stronger unit tests for seq-length classification, add perf gate in CI for dedicated profiles.
emma: thanks — great triage. Will update incident and close once hotfix is promoted. :thumbsup:
